# Pending changes (since patch 0001 "Streamed planets", 2026-11-06)

## Pirate raiders on planet surfaces (2026-11-06)
Asked for: the new pirate sprite (Downloads, "EVIL PIRATE ANDROID", 8 isometric
views) as a planet-surface NPC that wanders around shooting the player and other
NPCs except pirates, drops items on death; enough of them to make the surface
interesting; the player can attack pirates and pirates can attack the player.

What was done:
- Sprite: the sheet cut into art/pirate/pirate_idle_<dir>.png (8 views, 250-261 px,
  drawn 122 px tall like the guard). The sheet's 90° and 270° both face right, so
  West = East mirrored. One pose (rifle always up): SheetPuppet now falls back to
  the idle pictures when a sheet has no aim set. Source kept as
  external/images/npc_pirate_views.png.
- SurfacePirate (surface_props.gd): roams its band's camp (wander 520 px), looks
  for the nearest target every 0.25 s within 560 px - you or any citizen, never a
  pirate - and fires bursts of 3 red bolts (6 damage, 0.2 s apart, 1.2 s cool-down).
  70 health; in "surface_hostiles", so guards / archers / you shoot it. Clicked:
  a taunt instead of a conversation.
- Health for everyone on foot: citizens (guard 130, archer 95, pirate 70) flash red
  when hit, show a health bar once hurt, and fall (tilt, fade, freed) at 0; the
  surface's npc_died removes them and drops a pirate's loot. You: 100 health, a
  HUD bar under the credits (green -> red), regenerates 6/s after 4 s without a
  hit; at 0 knocked_out: back beside your ship, full health, 10% of credits gone.
  Pirates don't target you upstairs or on the stairs.
- Loot: LootDrop (glowing chest with a red light) where a pirate falls: 15-60
  credits, and 60% of the time 1-2 of scrap / energy cell / weapons / data core /
  alien alloy / medicine. Walk within 60 px to take it.
- Population (planned on the worker thread with the villages): 90 roaming bands of
  2-4 pirates across the planet (not within 30 tiles of the pad), plus a band of 3
  18-26 tiles from every village and a pair 30-38 tiles from the landing pad.
  Thalassa: 321 pirates planned, ~8 within reach at landing (nearest ~1700 px).
  They stream in with the citizens (within 64 tiles of you).
- Saved layouts keep pirates ([x, y, variant, "pirate"]).
- Maps: pirates are red dots on the minimap and planet map (legend "Pirates").
- Library (Characters room): a "PIRATE RAIDER" row walking in all 8 views; the
  scenery keeps clear of the new rows.
- Docs: pilot's guide (pirates, health, loot, knock-out); Talos docs (Library row).
- Tests: test_pirates (numbers, targeting never a pirate, hostile group, bolts hurt
  you, death -> loot -> collected, knock-out, citizens can fall);
  test_minoan_citizens ignores pirates; test_walk_into_and_out_of_buildings walks
  only the buildings in the path window at landing (walking streamed in a building
  beyond the window, which that hand-driven test can't route to). 60 tests pass.
- Measured: a pirate next to you took you from 100 to 82 health in ~3 s; you
  killed it; its chest gave 59 credits; knock-out took 10%.

Files changed (originals in base/): scripts/surface_props.gd, scripts/planet_surface.gd,
scripts/sheet_puppet.gd, scripts/surface_minimap.gd, scripts/surface_map.gd,
scripts/zoo.gd, tests/test_surface.gd, data/docs/game.md, data/docs/editor.md

New files: art/pirate/pirate_idle_{s,sw,w,nw,n,ne,e,se}.png,
external/images/npc_pirate_views.png

## Patch tracking that survives sessions (2026-11-06)
Asked for: a way to make sure the workflow is kept even if the session is lost, so
every change gets tracked and can be published in the game as a patch entry when ready.

What was done:
- tools/patch.py: tracking by snapshot instead of hand-made copies. `external/patcher/snapshot/`
  (every text file as of the last patch) + `manifest.json` (md5 of every tracked file,
  art included: 732 files) - changes are found by comparison, however they were made.
  Commands: status, notes-template, review (adds the code review to a patch entry;
  replaces tools/make_review.py), baseline (after publishing). The first baseline is
  the game as of patch 0001 (rebuilt: the pirate work shows as pending).
- CLAUDE.md (new): the workflow, read automatically by Claude Code in every session
  in this folder - track in pending.md after every change, publish only when asked,
  the publishing steps.
- Patcher: "Unpublished changes" at the top of the patch list (from external/patcher/ when
  running from the project): the log and the files changed since the last patch
  (found by md5 against the manifest).

Files changed: scripts/patcher.gd, tests/test_editor.gd, data/docs/editor.md
New files: tools/patch.py, CLAUDE.md, external/patcher/ (README.md, pending.md, snapshot/, manifest.json - not game files)

## Tracking folder moved to external/patcher (2026-11-06)
Asked for: move .patcher into the external folder as "patcher" - everything in
external/ is left out of builds.

What was done: .patcher/ -> external/patcher/ (pending.md, README.md, manifest.json,
snapshot/). It has a .gdignore so Godot doesn't import it (the snapshot holds copies of
the game's scripts - loaded as scripts they'd clash with the real ones); builds already
exclude external/* (export_presets.cfg, Linux and Windows). tools/patch.py, the
Patcher's "Unpublished changes", CLAUDE.md, the README and the Talos docs point to the
new place; tools/patch.py and the Patcher skip the folder when looking for changes.

Files changed: tools/patch.py, scripts/patcher.gd, CLAUDE.md, data/docs/editor.md, tests/test_editor.gd

## Shooting enemies on foot: click to attack (2026-11-06)
Asked for: "my player should be able to shoot enemies on surface".
(Firing existed - hold right-click on an enemy, or hold F - but it was easy to miss:
right-click only counted within 70 px of the enemy's middle (else the planet menu
opened), left-click walked up to "talk", and an enemy out of range just did nothing.)

What was done:
- Click an enemy - left or right button, anywhere on its figure (100 x 160 px box over
  its feet) - to attack it: out of range (700 px) you walk toward it (re-planned every
  0.4 s as it moves), in range you stand and fire until it falls. A click on the ground
  ends the fight; so does it getting away (1400 px), going upstairs or being knocked out.
- F attacks the nearest enemy (within twice your range) - "No enemy in sight." otherwise.
- Hovering an enemy: crosshair cursor and "<name> - click to attack".
- planet_surface.gd: attack / stop_attack / _update_attack (each frame), _hostile_at hit
  box, nearest_hostile(reach), input handling; the pilot's trigger is set while in range.
- Docs (pilot's guide): the controls. Tests: test_player_attacks_enemies (real mouse
  events: hover, a click on the head, closing in from 1000 px, firing, the kill, right-click,
  a click on the ground ends it, F) - a pirate at 1000 px went down in a few seconds.
- Found while testing: freeing a citizen node while it's still in the surface's npcs
  list crashes the engine (the game itself never does - _die removes it first); the
  test stands its other pirates aside instead.

Files changed: scripts/planet_surface.gd, tests/test_surface.gd, data/docs/game.md

## Pirate animation: raising the rifle and firing (2026-11-06)
Asked for: 4 new frames of the pirate (Downloads, pirate_frame_1..4.png) - raising the
gun and shooting it - to animate him, with the first frame as his idle pose when he
isn't attacking.

What was done:
- The four sheets (8 views each) cut automatically: the backdrop colour found per sheet,
  then the figures in each row (frame 3's sheet has a different layout and backdrop).
  Angle labels under the feet and specks removed; each frame scaled so its 8 views
  average 255 px (the frames come from sheets drawn at slightly different scales - the
  hat and feet mustn't jump between frames). As on every sheet, 90° and 270° both face
  right: East = 270°, West = East mirrored; 135° = north-east, 225° = north-west.
  art/pirate/pirate_{idle,raise1,raise2,aim}_<dir>.png (32 files, 252-257 px tall);
  sources kept as external/images/npc_pirate_frame_1..4.png. The old one-pose pictures
  (rifle always up) are replaced: idle is now frame 1, rifle down.
- SheetPuppet: a sheet's poses form a sequence idle, raise1, raise2..., aim (any
  <id>_raiseN_ frames found); raise_amt (0..1) picks the frame. Two-pose sheets (the
  guard) work as before.
- SurfacePirate: walk -> raise (0.45 s through frames 1-4) -> fire (bursts from frame 4)
  -> cool -> fire again if someone's still there, else lower (0.6 s, frames 4-1) ->
  walk with the rifle down. It can watch a single target (the Library's drone).
- Library: under the pirate's 8 walking views, its four frames side by side and a pirate
  raising its rifle and firing at a drone.
- Docs (Talos, Library). Tests: test_pirates checks the four-frame sequence, the idle
  frame when not attacking, and that raising runs idle -> raise1 -> raise2 -> aim.

Files changed: scripts/sheet_puppet.gd, scripts/surface_props.gd, scripts/zoo.gd,
tests/test_surface.gd, data/docs/editor.md
New files: art/pirate/pirate_{raise1,raise2,aim}_<dir>.png (24; the 8 idle ones replaced),
external/images/npc_pirate_frame_{1,2,3,4}.png

(Published as patch 0002 "Pirate raiders", 2026-11-06. While publishing: tools/patch.py
no longer counts new patch entries in data/patches/ as changes, and baseline archives
this log to history/<id>.md.)
